sections.html:
Waltham is a Middlesex County city on the Charles River, about 9 to 11 miles west of downtown Boston. The 2020 census counted 65,218 residents, and the 2024 estimate was 65,849.

It borders Watertown and Belmont to the east, Lexington to the north, Lincoln and Weston to the west, and Newton to the south. The city covers about 13.7 square miles, with around 12.7 square miles of land, and has ZIP codes 02451 to 02454.

The center of Waltham is the Common on Main Street, where City Hall, the public library and the post office stand. The river runs through town with several dams that once powered the mills.

sections.h2: Why is Waltham called the Watch City?
sections.html:
The Waltham Watch Company opened its factory here in 1854 and was the first to make watches on an assembly line. It produced over 35 million watches, clocks and instruments before it closed in 1957.

Waltham also hosted the Boston Manufacturing Company, whose model of mill and worker housing became known as the Waltham-Lowell system. The English settled the area in 1634 as part of Watertown, and Waltham became a separate town in 1738 and a city in 1884.

The city also holds large historic estates, including Gore Place (built in 1806), the Robert Treat Paine Estate and the 400-acre Lyman Estate.

Waltham grew quickly during the mill era, dipped after 1970, and has climbed again since 2000. Census figures show a peak of 61,582 in 1970, a fall to 57,878 by 1990 and a rise to 65,218 in 2020.

The 7.6 percent rise between 2010 and 2020 was the fastest since the 1960s. Population alone does not set a house price, so judge your own sale by the condition and location of the house.

Waltham is a patchwork of named villages, and each has its own character and housing mix. The list includes:

  • The Highlands, Piety Corner and Warrendale
  • The Bleachery, named for a former dye works, and The Chemistry, named for a former chemical company
  • Banks Square, Ellison Park, Cedarwood and Gardencrest
  • The Island, The Lanes, Ravenswood and Roberts
  • Kendal Green, mostly in Weston, and Wildwood Acres

Moody Street downtown has shops, restaurants and nightlife and is sometimes called Restaurant Row. Its access to the Commuter Rail and lower rents have drawn younger professionals in the twenty-first century. A seller near Moody Street can reasonably highlight that, while owners elsewhere may lean on quiet streets or the river trails.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in Waltham?
sections.html:
Waltham mixes universities, life sciences, utilities and corporate offices. The city's 2023 annual financial report lists the largest non-city employers as Bentley University, Brandeis University, Fresenius Medical Care, National Grid, Constant Contact and Vistaprint, each with 1,000 to 4,999 employees.

Others on the list include Eversource, MetLife and Sanofi Genzyme. Companies based in town include Revvity, RTX (headquarters of its Raytheon business), Thermo Fisher Scientific, Alkermes, Boston Dynamics and Pegasystems.

The city is also a base for regional offices. Wolverine World Wide moved its regional headquarters to the CityPoint campus in July 2016, and C & J Clark America moved to the former Polaroid site that October.

Retail concentrates on Main, Moody, Lexington and River Streets, parts of Route 60, the First Avenue area and a former Polaroid site that has seen new development. Because so many people work in town, owners with a job change, a divorce or an inherited house may need a quick answer on timing.

sections.h2: How do you get around Waltham?
sections.html:
Waltham is close to Interstate 95, which runs with Route 128 through the west of the city, and the Massachusetts Turnpike (I-90) is just south in Newton. Route 20 follows an old native trail called the Old Connecticut Path.

The MBTA Commuter Rail has two Waltham stops on the Fitchburg Line, one at Central Square across from City Hall and one near Brandeis. MBTA buses include routes 61, 70, 170, 505, 553, 554, 556 and 558. The Charles River path lets some residents bike to offices in Cambridge and Boston.

Distance to the train and to Route 128 sits near the top of most commuter buyers' lists, so list those distances when you sell. Wikipedia gives the city a walkability score of 62 out of 100 for central and south Waltham.

Waltham Public Schools run seven elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school. The elementary schools are Northeast, Fitzgerald, MacArthur, Plympton, Whittemore, Stanley and the Waltham Dual Language Elementary School.

The middle schools are McDevitt and Kennedy, and Waltham High School teams are the Hawks. Higher education includes Bentley and Brandeis, and private schools include Chapel Hill-Chauncy Hall and Gann Academy. The Waltham Times, a nonprofit online news outlet started in 2024, covers city news.

sections.h2: What does a Waltham seller need before closing?
sections.html:
A Waltham seller must obtain a certificate of compliance from the local fire department, showing the home's smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet state sale rules. The Waltham Fire Department has 166 full-time firefighters and a fire prevention division, so ask it how to schedule the inspection.

The Department of Fire Services recommends calling once you have a closing date. Requirements depend on the construction date and last permit date, and you can hire an electrician if hard-wired alarms need replacement.

On the title side, the state law library explains that Massachusetts has recorded land and registered land, with most deeds in the first group at the county Registry of Deeds. Attorneys are involved in most closings. For local permits, taxes and exemptions, ask the City of Waltham directly, since we did not confirm those details.

sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Waltham fast?
sections.html:
You can sell fast in Waltham by listing, selling privately or taking a cash offer, and a cash sale is usually the shortest path because it does not depend on a mortgage approval.

  • List: widest reach, but repairs, showings and a buyer's financing timeline
  • Private sale: lower fees, more of your time
  • Cash as-is: no prep, the offer reflects condition

Before you decide, it helps to line up three local contacts:

  • The assessors, for your property record card and any exemption on the bill
  • The building and inspection offices, for open permits and code questions
  • The Waltham Fire Department, for the alarm certificate appointment

Cash offers fit inherited houses, tenant issues, repairs you cannot afford and short deadlines. Always compare offers by your net, and we cannot guarantee a price before reviewing the house.

faqs.q: How far is Waltham from Boston?
faqs.a: Waltham is about 9 to 11 miles west of downtown Boston, depending on the measurement used.

faqs.q: What county is Waltham, MA in?
faqs.a: Waltham is in Middlesex County, Massachusetts.
Yes, two stops on the Fitchburg Line, one at Central Square and one near Brandeis University.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell my Waltham house?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a fire department certificate of compliance for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms when you sell or transfer a home.

faqs.q: Why is Waltham called the Watch City?
faqs.a: The Waltham Watch Company opened its factory in 1854 and was the first to make watches on an assembly line, producing over 35 million timepieces and instruments before closing in 1957.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Waltham house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses as they are, though any offer will reflect repairs the house needs.
